scenes.title: Recursive CTE
scenes.narration: A recursive CTE is a common table expression that references itself, letting you walk hierarchies and generate series that a single query could not express.

scenes.title: When to reach for recursion
bullets: Traversing hierarchies such as employee to manager chains.
Walking graph structures like folders or bill of materials.
Generating number or date series programmatically.
scenes.narration: Recursive CTEs shine when you need to traverse a hierarchy, such as following an employee up their chain of managers. They also handle general graph structures like nested folders or a bill of materials. Beyond hierarchies, they can generate sequences of numbers or dates on the fly.

scenes.title: The two required parts
steps: UNION ALL joins anchor to recursive member
Recursive member: references the CTE itself
Each pass feeds its output back in
Termination when the recursive member returns no rows
scenes.narration: Every recursive CTE has an anchor member that supplies the starting rows. It is combined with the recursive member using UNION ALL, and that recursive member refers back to the CTE itself. Each iteration feeds its output into the next pass until the recursive member returns no more rows and the recursion stops.

scenes.title: Employee to manager hierarchy
scenes.code:
WITH RECURSIVE org_chart AS (
    SELECT employee_id, first_name, manager_id, 1 AS level
    FROM employees
    WHERE manager_id IS NULL

    UNION ALL

    SELECT e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.manager_id, oc.level + 1
    FROM employees e
    JOIN org_chart oc ON e.manager_id = oc.employee_id
)
SELECT employee_id, first_name, level
FROM org_chart
ORDER BY level, employee_id;
scenes.narration: The anchor member selects the top of the org chart, the employees whose manager id is null, and marks them as level one. The recursive member joins the employees table back to the CTE, finding everyone who reports to a person already in the result and increasing the level by one. UNION ALL stitches each new layer onto the growing result until no more direct reports are found. The final query lists every employee with their depth in the hierarchy.

scenes.title: Generating a number series
scenes.code:
WITH RECURSIVE numbers AS (
    SELECT 1 AS n

    UNION ALL

    SELECT n + 1
    FROM numbers
    WHERE n < 10
)
SELECT n
FROM numbers;
scenes.narration: This recursive CTE builds the numbers one through ten without any source table. The anchor starts at one, and the recursive member adds one each pass. The WHERE clause is the crucial termination condition, stopping the recursion once n reaches ten.

scenes.text: Always include a termination condition in the recursive member. Without one, the CTE loops forever, and engines apply a recursion depth limit that will abort the query.
scenes.narration: Never omit the termination condition in the recursive member, or the CTE will loop endlessly. Most engines impose a maximum recursion depth and will abort the query once that limit is exceeded.
